chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Bazie, from Mansur ibn Yunus, from Abu Bakr al-Hadrami, from Abu Ja'far and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
That they both said: 'Salat is not broken except by four things: defecation, urination, passing wind, and sound (speaking).'
ai.seo_question: What are the four things that break the prayer (Salat) in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith, transmitted through the chain of the Six Companions (Al-Sittah) to the Imams, establishes a minimalist criterion for nullifying prayer, contrasting with broader juristic opinions that include laughter or eating. By limiting the invalidators to excretion, urination, wind, and vocal speech, it emphasizes the continuity of devotion unless a significant physical or auditory distraction occurs. This ruling reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on ease in worship, ensuring that minor distractions do not unnecessarily break the spiritual connection during Salāt.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, and Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Muhammad Bin Ismail Bin Bazie, from Mansour Bin Yunus, from Abu Bakr Al Hazramy, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> and Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>
, both of themasws were saying: ‘The Salāt does not get cut off except by four – the faeces, and the urine, and the wind, and the sound (talking)’.
en.sarwar: 4. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn ’Isma‘il ibn Bazi‘ from Mansur ibn Yunus from abu Bakr al-Hadramiy who has said the following: “Abu Ja‘far, and abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhim al-Salam, would say, ‘
Only four things discontinue Salah (prayer): defecation, urination, gas and sound.’”
